messages:
maria: Heads up — we just saw a ~3x p99 token latency spike on prod around 09:12 UTC for the gpt-small-quant family. Affecting streaming endpoints and increasing client timeouts.
kevin: Is this global or a region?
maria: Looks US-west primary, but a few routed requests in eu-west saw elevated tails too.
ci-bot: deploy-notice: canary deploy 2026-03-18T08:55 by ci-pipeline completed for runtime v2.14.7
kevin: Any correlation with the canary?
maria: Canary started 08:55; spike started ~09:12. But canary was limited to 1% — graphs don't show obvious alloc spikes from canary.
olga: grabbed a flame + profiler dump for a stuck request. Early signal: kernel selection is frequently choosing the "generic_attention" kernel instead of the optimized "small-seq-attn" for sequences ~24-48 tokens. That increases per-token latency significantly. Snippet of kernel logs:
```
[09:12:34] kernel_selector: seq_len=32, batch_size=4 -> chosen_kernel=generic_attention (score: 0.78)
[09:12:34] kernel_selector: seq_len=16, batch_size=2 -> chosen_kernel=generic_attention (score: 0.81)
[09:12:34] fallback_reason=shape_mismatch_threshold exceeded: var_seq_ratio=0.55
```
kevin: Why would seq_len be small-ish and still go generic?
olga: We saw a sudden rise in very short but frequent requests — looks like a tool-calling loop from a single tenant that calls tools repeatedly and streams small chunks, which makes the per-batch variance high and selector's variance metric triggers fallback.
sam: Do we have kvcache metrics? If streaming small chunks and not reusing prefixes, kvcache churn could explain extra work.
maria: Yep — kvcache evictions shot up at the same time. From the node: 
```
kvcache_stats: hits=4800 miss=19800 evict_ops=12400 max_size=512MB cur_size=498MB
kvcache_eviction_rate: 24.9/s (baseline ~1.2/s)
```
kevin: Oof. High eviction rate + generic kernel = double cost. Any tenant id?
olga: traced patterns; noisy tenant id=tn-7e9b. Their request signature shows a tool-call loop with many streaming chunks: "tool:search -> tool:extract -> tool:search ..." short prompts appended.
lucas: That pattern will break batching heuristics too — micro-batches, high variance -> weight towards conservative kernels.
sam: Is noisy neighbor capacity isolation tripping? queues?
maria: Queue depth for the GPU worker nodes rose ~30% for that tenant's shard. Not full saturation but enough to increase scheduling jitter.
kevin: Prioritize mitigation: 1) throttle tenant, 2) temporarily prefer small-seq kernels for seq_len <= 64, 3) reduce kvcache evictions by increasing cache TTL for recently used prefixes. Thoughts?
olga: Patch for kernel selector is small — change var_seq_ratio threshold from 0.5 -> 0.8 for the affected model family. I can ship a hotfix to canary now.
lucas: For kvcache TTL we need config push to routing layer. We can bump TTL for the model family or add a per-tenant override. Per-tenant looks better.
sam: Throttle tenant tn-7e9b at the routing policy (rate-limit and stream concurrency=1) and open a ticket with infra to SIG-tenant. I'll do a quick ACL throttle so it doesn't impact others.
ci-bot: incident:perf created (INC-2026-213): "latency spike — kernel selection & kvcache churn" assigned to eng-runtime oncall
maria: Action list:
- sam: apply temporary tenant throttle (now ETA 5m)
- olga: push kernel selector canary change to canary pool (ETA 10m)
- lucas: config change for per-tenant kvcache TTL (ETA 20m)
- kevin: monitor p99/p50, eviction_rate, kernel-choice ratio; if not improved revert changes (ETA 30m)
kevin: After throttle applied p99 dropped ~60% in 4m; eviction_rate down to 3.4/s. Looks promising.
olga: canary kernel selector change pushed; canary instances report chosen_kernel switches to small-seq-attn for the spike workload.
lucas: p99 still slightly elevated for streaming endpoints (1.2x baseline) — suspect streaming backpressure from existing connections. We should add a short-term reduce-stream-buffering flag to accept smaller buffers for these tenants.
sam: Throttle + canary + TTL bump seems to have stabilized most playback. I'll leave throttle for 1h and then dial up slowly while we look at root cause.
maria: Root cause summary (for postmortem): tenant-induced tool-calling loop created a high-variance short-sequence workload. Kernel selector's variance-based safety triggered fallback to generic kernels, while KV cache eviction thrash increased work per token. Combined with queue jitter produced 3x p99.
olga: Long-term fixes: improve kernel selector to consider recent sequence-length histograms per-tenant; add per-tenant kvcache policies; add a backpressure signal from streaming layer to routing to prevent tool-call tight loops; and add alert for sudden kvcache eviction spikes.
kevin: I'll draft the postmortem and include perf profiles + quick graphs. Good job on the triage team. :clap:
